title: Game reconstruction and tools discovery
summary: Review 25 game reconstructions and game-specific research tools.
notes: Personally compared current catalogue and discovery sources, examined primary READMEs pinned to repository commits and inspected source trees. No independent builds, gameplay or binary comparisons. Amiga and Atari ST searches primarily returned tracked projects or forks; the accepted batch is predominantly DOS.

sources.reason: Native C++ engine rebuilt from the DOS VGA program; author reports playable behavior using original game files.
C++ engine aiming to reproduce the DOS game using original data; its README describes an accuracy goal, not independent verification.
C# tools and format notes for extracting and inspecting game archives, sprites and maps.
Browser reconstruction with extracted original levels and author-described oracle comparison using an emulator for testing, not as the game runtime.
Assembly patcher and root-cause analysis for mass-driver faults, plus an autosave feature.
Browser game with jump physics reconstructed from the DOS executable; the author reports frame-by-frame comparison.
Documents the game installation, EXEPACK image and level and score formats with reproducible analysis tools.
Documents game files and image formats with analysis scripts; original game files are not included.
Extracts and repacks game resources and supports image conversion and executable patching.
Extracts and converts graphics, sounds and other resources from the DOS game.
Extracts DOS game archives, including graphics, sounds and music.
Extracts DOS game archives, graphics, sounds and music.
Extracts IPW archives and converts PIC images to PNG.
In-development sprite extractor; author notes bugs and incomplete extraction.
Python graphics extractor for both versions of the DOS game.
C++ extractor for Raptor GLB archives.
Python extraction of EGA tiles from the DOS game.
DOS level editor for Paranoid 1.8, including test-play and level manipulation.
Save editor with Python and Swift implementations; author explicitly credits Claude Code.
C# save editor; the author notes that item editing is not implemented.
Java viewer and editor for the DOS game’s LEVEL file.
Reverse-engineered DOS formats with asset extraction, viewing and repacking tools.
Reverse-engineered game formats and an unfinished terrain and texture editor.
Tools unpack and repack game resource archives; source release platform is not established by the inspected README.
Utilities extract and repack game data from WINTER.EXE and WINTER2.BIN.
